items.descriptionTR:
Pontiff calls on leaders to treat migrants more humanely as he concludes week-long Spanish tour in Gran Canaria
The constant flow of people embarking in small, rickety boats to migrate abroad should force a reckoning as to why we have built a world where so many “must risk death to seek life”, Pope Leo has said as he warned: “We cannot grow accustomed to counting the dead.”
Thursday’s speech in the Canary Islands, on the final leg of the pontiff’s week-long tour of Spain, contained Leo’s most pointed comments to date on migration.
items.titleTR: Pope Leo rails against migrant deaths on visit to Spain’s ‘dock of shame’

￼
US Central Command (CENTCOM) confirmed a fresh wave of “self-defense strikes” directly hitting radar, surveillance, and military facilities in southern Iran. Credit: CENTCOM
For the second straight day, the US and Iran have traded retaliatory military strikes across the Middle East, pushing an already fragile April ceasefire to the brink of collapse.
US Central Command (CENTCOM) confirmed a fresh wave of “self-defense strikes” directly hitting radar, surveillance, and military facilities in southern Iran. The American bombardment followed a stark warning from US President Donald Trump, who declared that Washington would hit Iran “hard” because Tehran had taken “too long to make a deal” to halt hostilities permanently.
Iran is being hit harder than anything we’ve seen. ￼ pic.twitter.com/bwvB2aYaFJ
— USA NEWS ￼ (@usanewshq) June 11, 2026

Iran targets US bases in the Middle East
Tehran immediately struck back, targeting US military infrastructure across multiple neighboring countries. For a second consecutive day, American bases in Kuwait and Bahrain faced Iranian fire, while Iranian state media reported that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) launched ballistic missiles at a US command center in Jordan. The attacks forced Kuwait to temporarily shut down its airspace after its military intercepted “hostile aerial targets,” while air raid sirens sounded in the middle of the night in Bahrain.
The conflict has also spilled into vital global shipping lanes. Iranian state media claimed the IRGC struck two oil tankers and declared the strategic Strait of Hormuz “completely closed.” While CENTCOM countered that commercial maritime traffic was still successfully transiting the waterway, global energy markets panicked. Brent crude quickly jumped 2%, surging to around $95 a barrel.
The escalating rhetoric suggests no immediate end to the violence. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth warned that bombs would continue to drop on Iran’s core facilities if a diplomatic resolution isn’t reached, a sentiment echoed by President Trump on Truth Social.
Meanwhile, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stood defiant, vowing that Iran “will stand firm against any pressure or threat” while slamming Washington for sabotaging peace talks with contradictory diplomacy.
items.titleTR: Ceasefire Shattered: US and Iran Trade Heavy Strikes for Second Day

items.titleTR: Scientists discover where whales go to die

items.descriptionTR: Dans une étude publiée mercredi 10 juin dans «Nature», des scientifiques révèlent avoir découvert des squelettes de baleines à 7 000 mètres de profondeur à l’ouest de l’Australie. Certains sont vieux de 5,3 millions d’années.
items.titleTR: «D’une importance majeure pour comprendre leur évolution» : un cimetière de près de 500 baleines découvert au fond de l’océan Indien

slots.packetSpot: Recent discoveries of whale graveyards in the Indian Ocean have provided scientists with significant insights into whale evolution and their final resting places. These findings are crucial for understanding the life cycle and migratory patterns of these marine giants.
slots.packetTitle: Discovery of Whale Graveyards in the Indian Ocean Provides Evolutionary Insights

items.descriptionTR: Dozens of motorcycle taxi drivers rode through eastern DR Congo carrying Ebola prevention messages as health officials seek to combat misinformation and scepticism amid a growing outbreak.
items.titleTR: Congo motorcyclists mobilise as Ebola outbreak fuels fear

items.descriptionTR: The scaling back of development aid has contributed to the inability to contain the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. German organizations are calling for a major spending boost to help stop the spread.
items.titleTR: International aid cuts complicate Congo's Ebola epidemic

slots.packetSpot: The Ebola outbreak in Congo is causing widespread concern, with local communities mobilizing, international aid facing cuts, and new cases emerging.
slots.packetTitle: Congo's Ebola Outbreak: Local Mobilization, Aid Challenges, and Emerging Cases

items.descriptionTR: Warnings of a powerful El Nino weather pattern this year suggest that we may be about to face drought, flooding and extreme heat. What impacts are in store? And can we prepare for the worst of it?
items.titleTR: The strongest El Nino in more than a century may be coming

items.descriptionTR: D’après la vigie américaine de l’océan, le phénomène climatique naturel, synonyme de sécheresses, inondations et températures records dans le monde, s’est bien installé dans le Pacifique tropical. Les experts estiment à 63 % le risque d’un épisode très fort entre novembre et janvier.
items.titleTR: El Niño, «l’enfant terrible du Pacifique», a officiellement commencé

slots.packetSpot: Meteorological reports confirm the official start of an El Niño event, with predictions suggesting it could be the strongest in over a century. This climate phenomenon is expected to have significant global impacts.
slots.packetTitle: The Onset of a Potentially Historic El Niño Event
